question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

 

Beat around the bush
option_2: To avoid getting to the point of an issue
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. To avoid getting to the point of an issue.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Beat around the bush is an idiom that means to avoid talking about what is really important, or to delay coming to the main point of a discussion. (बात को घुमाना फिराना)

◦ Example: Stop beating around the bush and tell me what happened at the meeting.

 

• The idiom is believed to have originated from hunting, where beaters would strike bushes to drive birds out into the open without directly approaching the danger themselves — hence the sense of avoiding the direct/central issue.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: To speak rashly — means to speak hastily or without thinking; it describes a manner of speaking, not evasion of a topic.

 

• Option 3: To speak abusively — means to speak rudely or insultingly, which is unrelated to avoiding a point.

 

• Option 4: To speak convincingly — means to speak persuasively; this is the opposite of evading an issue.

 

NOTE

 

• Other frequently asked idioms with similar sense of evasion: hem and haw (to be hesitant/indecisive in speech), skirt an issue (to avoid dealing with something directly).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

The inclusion of Durga Puja in the UNESCO's list of Intangible Cultural Heritage was only possible due to the arduous _______ of all stakeholders.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. efforts.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Arduous (adjective) means requiring strenuous or sustained effort; difficult and tiring. (कठिन, श्रमसाध्य) It naturally collocates with words like effort(s), task, journey.

◦ Example: Climbing the mountain was an arduous task that required the arduous efforts of the entire team.

 

• The sentence needs a noun that can be described as arduous and that was made of all stakeholders — i.e., a collective exertion. Only efforts fits this sense of hard work put in collectively.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: passivity — means inactivity or lack of initiative; the opposite of the strenuous exertion implied by ‘arduous’, so it does not fit.

 

• Option 3: affects — ‘affects’ is a verb (to influence), and even the noun ‘effects’ (results) does not fit the sense of collective exertion required here.

 

• Option 4: ignorance — means lack of knowledge; it cannot be described as ‘arduous’ and does not fit the context of stakeholders working together.

 

NOTE

 

• Do not confuse affect (verb, to influence) with effect (noun, a result) — a very common SSC error-spotting trap.

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

 

The bishop sadly declared that the poor gentleman who was dead was quieter of the community.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. the quietest.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Degrees of comparison: the comparative degree (‘quieter’, ‘more quiet’) is used to compare exactly two persons/things, while the superlative degree (‘the quietest’, ‘the most quiet’) is used when comparing three or more persons/things or one person/thing with the rest of a group.

◦ Example: Of the two brothers, Raj is the taller. / Of all the students in the class, Raj is the tallest.

 

• Here the gentleman is being compared with the whole community (a group of many people), so the superlative degree must be used, and ‘of’ (not ‘than’) precedes the group being compared — ‘the quietest of the community’.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: the quieter — this is still the comparative degree, which is incorrect when comparing one person to an entire group (community).

 

• Option 2: quiet — this is the positive degree (no comparison at all), which cannot express ‘the most quiet member of the community’.

 

• Option 4: most quiet — ‘quiet’ is a one-syllable adjective and forms its superlative by adding ‘-est’ (quietest); ‘most’ is used only with adjectives of two or more syllables (e.g., most beautiful), so ‘most quiet’ is an incorrect formation.

 

NOTE

 

• Rule for degree formation: one-syllable adjectives take -er/-est (tall–taller–tallest); most two-or-more-syllable adjectives take more/most (beautiful–more beautiful–most beautiful); comparatives are followed by ‘than’, superlatives by ‘of/in’.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

 

In addition with / the existing crisis in economy, / the rise of hunger index / is another cause of worry.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. In addition with.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In addition to is a fixed prepositional phrase meaning ‘besides’ or ‘as well as’. The preposition that follows ‘addition’ in this phrase is always ‘to’, never ‘with’.

◦ Example: In addition to his salary, he receives a travel allowance.

 

• Hence, ‘In addition with the existing crisis…’ is grammatically wrong; it must read ‘In addition to the existing crisis…’.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: the rise of hunger index — grammatically correct as used; no error.

 

• Option 2: the existing crisis in economy — grammatically correct as used; no error.

 

• Option 3: is another cause of worry — grammatically correct subject-verb agreement (singular subject ‘the rise’ takes ‘is’); no error.

 

NOTE

 

• Other fixed preposition combinations frequently tested by SSC: similar to, different from, married to, proud of, consist of.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Machinary.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct spelling of the word is Machinery (मशीनरी) — machines collectively, or the working parts of a machine. The given word ‘Machinary’ is misspelt (incorrect vowel ‘a’ in place of ‘e’).

◦ Example: The factory installed new machinery last month.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Hymn — correctly spelt; means a religious song of praise.

 

• Option 3: Idol — correctly spelt; means an object of worship/a person greatly admired.

 

• Option 4: Motto — correctly spelt; means a short sentence expressing a guiding principle.

 

NOTE

 

• Commonly misspelt SSC words: machinery, questionnaire, embarrass, occurrence, definitely, perseverance, rhythm.

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

 

The moment James saw Regena, he fell head on to his heels in love with her.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. head over heels.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Head over heels (in love) is a fixed idiom meaning completely or deeply in love. (पूरी तरह से (प्यार में डूबा हुआ))

◦ Example: She fell head over heels in love with him the moment they met.

 

• The idiom is a fixed collocation — none of its words can be substituted, reordered, or replaced (‘head on to his heels’ in the original sentence is a corrupted, non-idiomatic form).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: heels of the head — not an English idiom; meaningless in this context.

 

• Option 2: head and heels — an incorrect, non-idiomatic variation of the fixed phrase.

 

• Option 3: heads in the heels — not a recognised idiom; grammatically and idiomatically incorrect.

 

NOTE

 

• Other idioms involving body parts frequently asked by SSC: heart and soul (with total commitment), head and shoulders above (far superior to), keep one's head (stay calm).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

 

Most probably, / he come / to office / next Tuesday.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. he come.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The sentence refers to a plan for ‘next Tuesday’, a future time expression, so the verb must be in the simple future tense (will/shall + base form). The bare present form ‘come’ used with the third-person singular subject ‘he’ is incorrect here.

◦ Example: Most probably, he will come to office next Tuesday.

 

• Even without the future time marker, ‘he come’ would violate basic subject–verb agreement in the simple present, where third-person singular subjects take the ‘-s/-es’ form (he comes).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: next Tuesday — a correctly formed time adverbial; no error.

 

• Option 3: to office — correct prepositional phrase; no error.

 

• Option 4: most probably — correct adverbial phrase of probability; no error.

 

NOTE

 

• When a sentence contains a clear future time marker (tomorrow, next week, next Tuesday, soon), the verb should generally be in a future form — this is a frequently tested SSC error-spotting pattern.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

 

Pacify
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Enrage.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pacify (verb) means to calm someone down, or to ease anger/hostility. (शांत करना)

◦ Example: The mother tried to pacify her crying child.

 

• Enrage means to make someone extremely angry — the direct opposite of calming someone down. (क्रोधित करना)

◦ Example: The unfair decision enraged the entire workforce.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Restore — means to bring back to an original state; unrelated to calming anger.

 

• Option 2: Negate — means to nullify or make ineffective; unrelated to anger/calmness.

 

• Option 4: Amuse — means to entertain or make someone laugh; not the opposite of ‘pacify’.

 

NOTE

 

• Synonyms of pacify: appease, placate, soothe, mollify, calm; Antonyms: enrage, incense, provoke, infuriate, agitate.

question:
Read the following sentence and select its future tense form from the following options.

 

The food company promoted newly launched products at affordable prices.
option_1: The food company will be promoting newly launched products at affordable prices.
option_2: The food company promotes newly launched products at affordable prices.
option_3: The food company had promoted newly launched products at affordable prices.
option_4: The food company is promoting newly launched products at affordable prices.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. The food company will be promoting newly launched products at affordable prices.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The question asks for the future tense form of the given simple-past sentence. Among the four options, only one uses a future-tense structure (‘will be’ + verb-ing, the future continuous form); the rest are all non-future tenses.

 

• Future continuous tense is formed as: Subject + will/shall + be + V-ing.

◦ Example: The food company will be promoting newly launched products at affordable prices.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: The food company promotes… — this is in the simple present tense, not the future.

 

• Option 3: The food company had promoted… — this is in the past perfect tense, not the future.

 

• Option 4: The food company is promoting… — this is in the present continuous tense, not the future.

 

NOTE

 

• Tense structures: Simple future — will/shall + V1; Future continuous — will be + V-ing; Future perfect — will have + V3; Future perfect continuous — will have been + V-ing.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence.

 

Reduced price of cooking gas brought happy to the face of every citizen.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. happiness.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The verb ‘brought’ needs a noun as its direct object (something that is ‘brought’ to the face). ‘Happy’ is an adjective and cannot function as a noun/object, so it must be replaced by the noun form ‘happiness’. (खुशी)

◦ Example: Reduced price of cooking gas brought happiness to the face of every citizen.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: happier — the comparative form of the adjective ‘happy’; still an adjective, so it cannot serve as the object of ‘brought’.

 

• Option 2: happiest — the superlative form of the adjective ‘happy’; still an adjective and grammatically unsuitable as a noun object.

 

• Option 3: happily — this is an adverb (modifies a verb/adjective), not a noun, so it cannot be the object of ‘brought’.

 

NOTE

 

• Word family: happy (adjective) → happiness (noun) → happily (adverb) → happier/happiest (comparative/superlative adjective).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

 

Rishi Sunak, the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom and Leader of the Conservative Party, was born into Southampton to parents of Indian descent who immigrated to Britain from East Africa in the 1960s.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. was born in.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The preposition ‘in’ is used with ‘born’ to indicate the place (city/country) of birth: ‘born in’ + place. ‘Born into’ is used with a family, social class, or situation one is born into (e.g., born into poverty), not a place name like ‘Southampton’.

◦ Example: Rishi Sunak was born in Southampton.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: was born on — ‘born on’ is used with a specific date (e.g., born on 12 May), not with a place name.

 

• Option 2: No substitution required — incorrect, because ‘was born into Southampton’ is grammatically wrong as it stands; a correction is required.

 

• Option 4: was born with — ‘born with’ is used with an inherent trait or quality (e.g., born with a talent), not with a place.

 

NOTE

 

• Preposition + ‘born’ combinations: born in (place/year), born on (date), born into (family/class/situation), born with (trait/quality).

question:
Select the most appropriate adverb to fill in the blank.

 

The explorers trekked _________ through the dense jungle.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. bravely.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An adverb of manner describes how an action is performed. The sentence describes how the explorers trekked through a dense (and presumably dangerous) jungle, so a manner adverb describing courage — ‘bravely’ (बहादुरी से) — fits best.

◦ Example: The explorers trekked bravely through the dense jungle.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: before — an adverb of time; it does not describe the manner of trekking and does not fit the sentence sense.

 

• Option 2: rarely — an adverb of frequency; it does not describe manner and would contradict the descriptive intent of the sentence.

 

• Option 3: ever — an adverb of frequency/degree, generally used in questions, negatives, or comparisons; it does not fit an affirmative descriptive statement here.

 

NOTE

 

• Categories of adverbs frequently tested by SSC: manner (bravely, quickly, slowly), time (now, before, soon), frequency (often, rarely, ever), place (here, there, everywhere).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the bracketed word to fill in the blank.

 

The rainbow arched gracefully across the sky, painting it in _________ (lifeless) hues.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. vibrant.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lifeless (adjective) means dull, without energy or colour; showing no sign of life. (निर्जीव, फीका)

 

• Vibrant means full of life, bright and striking in colour — the direct opposite of ‘lifeless’, and it fits perfectly with the context of a colourful rainbow. (जीवंत, चमकीला)

◦ Example: The rainbow arched gracefully across the sky, painting it in vibrant hues.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: spiritual — relates to the soul/religion; unrelated in meaning to ‘lifeless’ or its opposite.

 

• Option 3: ashless — not a standard, meaningful English word in this context; a distractor.

 

• Option 4: muted — means soft or subdued (of colour/sound); this is close in meaning to ‘lifeless/dull’, not its opposite.

 

NOTE

 

• Synonyms of lifeless: dull, inanimate, lackluster, drab; Antonyms: vibrant, vivid, lively, animated, spirited.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

 

My sister Mona / never drinks coffee; / she prefer tea / in the morning.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. she prefer tea.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Subject–verb agreement: in the simple present tense, a singular subject (he/she/it or a singular noun) takes a verb with ‘-s/-es’ added to it. The subject ‘she’ requires ‘prefers’, not the bare form ‘prefer’.

◦ Example: My sister Mona never drinks coffee; she prefers tea in the morning.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: My sister Mona — a correctly formed noun phrase (subject); no error.

 

• Option 2: never drinks coffee; — correct subject-verb agreement (drinks, third-person singular); no error.

 

• Option 3: in the morning — a correct prepositional phrase of time; no error.

 

NOTE

 

• Rule: with third-person singular subjects in the simple present, verbs add -s (drinks, likes) or -es (goes, watches, prefers is an exception in spelling but takes -s: prefer + s = prefers).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

 

The team was gradually realising that the social gatherings were draining.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. absorbing.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Draining (adjective) describes something that leaves a person feeling exhausted or worn out — tedious and energy-sapping. (थका देने वाला)

 

• Absorbing describes something so engaging and interesting that it fully holds one's attention, leaving one engaged rather than exhausted — the intended opposite sense here. (आकर्षक, तल्लीन करने वाला)

◦ Example: The team was gradually realising that the social gatherings were absorbing.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: unfruitful — means unproductive; it does not express the opposite of ‘tiring/draining’.

 

• Option 2: flippant — means not showing due seriousness; unrelated to the energy/engagement sense of ‘draining’.

 

• Option 3: frivolous — means not serious or silly; again unrelated to the intended opposite of ‘draining’.

 

NOTE

 

• In SSC vocabulary questions, ‘draining’ (tiresome/exhausting) is commonly paired as an antonym with words expressing positive engagement such as absorbing, engaging, invigorating, refreshing.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the highlighted word in the given sentence.

 

The author's writing style is characterised by a subtle and nuanced use of language.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Elaborate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Subtle (adjective) means understated, delicately indirect, not obvious or elaborate. (सूक्ष्म, अस्पष्ट)

 

• Elaborate means highly detailed, complicated, or worked out with great care — the opposite of something understated/subtle. (विस्तृत, जटिल)

◦ Example: The author's writing style is characterised by an elaborate and ornate use of language.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Elegant — means gracefully stylish; it does not express the opposite of ‘subtle’.

 

• Option 2: Sturdy — means strong and solidly built; an unrelated quality with no connection to ‘subtle’.

 

• Option 3: Delicate — means fine, mild or subtle in itself; this is close in meaning to ‘subtle’, not its opposite.

 

NOTE

 

• Synonyms of subtle: delicate, understated, nuanced; Antonyms: obvious, blatant, elaborate, overt.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

 

Delay
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Hasten.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Delay (verb) means to make something happen later than planned; to postpone or slow down. (देरी करना)

◦ Example: Heavy rain delayed the flight by two hours.

 

• Hasten means to hurry or speed something up — the direct opposite of delaying. (जल्दी करना)

◦ Example: She hastened her steps to catch the train.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Wait — means to remain in a place until something happens; it is close in sense to ‘delay’, not its opposite.

 

• Option 2: Lag — means to fall behind, to move slowly; again close in meaning to ‘delay’, not opposite.

 

• Option 3: Intervene — means to become involved in a situation to change its outcome; unrelated to speed/delay.

 

NOTE

 

• Synonyms of delay: postpone, defer, procrastinate, stall, lag; Antonyms: hasten, expedite, accelerate, hurry, quicken.

question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence.

 

Many biologists have stated the fact that most of the herbs are perinnial and have healing qualities with added flavour.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Perinnial.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct spelling is Perennial (बारहमासी, चिरस्थायी) — lasting a long time or recurring again and again; (of plants) living for more than two years. The given word ‘Perinnial’ is misspelt (incorrect vowels).

◦ Example: Most of the herbs in the garden are perennial and flower every year.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Healing — correctly spelt.

 

• Option 2: Biologists — correctly spelt.

 

• Option 3: Qualities — correctly spelt.

 

NOTE

 

• Words commonly confused/misspelt with ‘perennial’: perennial vs. biennial vs. annual (relating to how often a plant completes its life cycle).

question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence.

 

The neighbour came in disgoise and attacked her children.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. disgoise.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct spelling is disguise (भेष बदलना/छद्मवेश) — to change one's appearance to hide one's identity. The given word ‘disgoise’ is misspelt (incorrect vowel combination ‘oi’ in place of ‘ui’).

◦ Example: The neighbour came in disguise and attacked her children.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: children — correctly spelt.

 

• Option 2: attacked — correctly spelt.

 

• Option 3: neighbour — correctly spelt (British spelling, generally preferred in SSC exams; the American variant is ‘neighbor’).

 

NOTE

 

• Other ‘gui/gue’-pattern words often tested for spelling: guide, guitar, guess, guarantee, guardian.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

In order to maintain good governance, every government servant must be held _____ for his/her decisions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. accountable.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Accountable (adjective) means required or expected to justify one's actions or decisions; responsible/answerable. (जवाबदेह) It commonly occurs in the fixed collocation ‘held accountable for’.

◦ Example: Every government servant must be held accountable for his/her decisions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: irresponsible — means not showing a proper sense of responsibility; this is the opposite of what good governance requires.

 

• Option 3: flexible — means adaptable/willing to change; it does not fit the context of taking responsibility for decisions.

 

• Option 4: unaccountable — means not required to justify one's actions; this contradicts the sentence's intent of ensuring good governance.

 

NOTE

 

• Related words often tested together: accountable, answerable, responsible, liable — all can combine with ‘held … for’.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. (Que. No. 21-25)

 

We're a society fixated on numbers. So, it's no (1)_______ we use measurements and equations to score our weight. The most (2)_______ is BMI, a measure of our body weight to height ratio. BMI (3)_______ bodies as underweight, normal or healthy weight, overweight or obese and can be a useful tool for weight and health (4)_______. But it shouldn't be used as the single (5)_______ of what it means to be a healthy weight when we set our weight loss goals.

 

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. surprise.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The passage uses the fixed expression ‘it's no surprise (that) …’, meaning ‘it is not surprising that …’, to introduce an unsurprising fact — here, that a numbers-obsessed society uses measurements and equations to score body weight.

◦ Example: It's no surprise we use measurements and equations to score our weight.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: resolution — means a firm decision; ‘it's no resolution we use…’ does not make sense grammatically or contextually.

 

• Option 3: vibrance — means liveliness/brightness; it does not fit the fixed expression or the sense of the sentence.

 

• Option 4: persistence — means continued firm effort; it does not fit the fixed expression ‘it's no ___ we…’.

 

NOTE

 

• Fixed expressions with ‘surprise’ frequently used in SSC passages: it comes as no surprise, to my surprise, take by surprise.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. (Que. No. 21-25)

 

We're a society fixated on numbers. So, it's no (1)_______ we use measurements and equations to score our weight. The most (2)_______ is BMI, a measure of our body weight to height ratio. BMI (3)_______ bodies as underweight, normal or healthy weight, overweight or obese and can be a useful tool for weight and health (4)_______. But it shouldn't be used as the single (5)_______ of what it means to be a healthy weight when we set our weight loss goals.

 

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. popular.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The passage states that BMI is ‘the most (2) is BMI, a measure of our body weight to height ratio’ — BMI is described as the most widely used/common measure, i.e., the most popular one, which logically leads into it being explained as ‘a measure of our body weight to height ratio’ in the same sentence.

◦ Example: The most popular is BMI, a measure of our body weight to height ratio.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: uncharted — means unexplored/unknown; this contradicts BMI being a well-known, widely used measure.

 

• Option 3: indistinct — means unclear/vague; BMI is a clearly defined numerical measure, so this does not fit.

 

• Option 4: imprecise — means inexact; while BMI is sometimes criticised as imprecise, the sentence here is simply introducing it as a widely used measure, so ‘popular’ fits the context better.

 

NOTE

 

• BMI (Body Mass Index) = weight (kg) / [height (m)]²; it is a widely used but limited screening tool for weight categories.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. (Que. No. 21-25)

 

We're a society fixated on numbers. So, it's no (1)_______ we use measurements and equations to score our weight. The most (2)_______ is BMI, a measure of our body weight to height ratio. BMI (3)_______ bodies as underweight, normal or healthy weight, overweight or obese and can be a useful tool for weight and health (4)_______. But it shouldn't be used as the single (5)_______ of what it means to be a healthy weight when we set our weight loss goals.

 

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. classifies.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Classify means to arrange or categorise things into groups based on shared characteristics. (वर्गीकृत करना) The passage explains that BMI classifies bodies as underweight, normal or healthy weight, overweight or obese — a clear act of categorisation.

◦ Example: BMI classifies bodies as underweight, normal or healthy weight, overweight or obese.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: dissuades — means discourages; it does not fit the sense of categorising bodies into weight groups.

 

• Option 2: speculates — means to form a theory/guess without firm evidence; BMI is a defined calculation, not a guess.

 

• Option 4: meanders — means to wander aimlessly; it does not fit the sense of systematically categorising bodies.

 

NOTE

 

• Words of categorisation frequently used in SSC comprehension passages: classify, categorise, group, sort.

We're a society fixated on numbers. So, it's no (1)_______ we use measurements and equations to score our weight. The most (2)_______ is BMI, a measure of our body weight to height ratio. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. screening.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Screening (noun) means the process of testing or examining someone/something for a particular purpose, especially in a medical/health context. (जांच) BMI being ‘a useful tool for weight and health screening’ fits naturally, as BMI is used to screen/assess health-related weight status.

◦ Example: BMI can be a useful tool for weight and health screening.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: planting — relates to agriculture; wholly unrelated to weight/health assessment.

 

• Option 3: landing — relates to aircraft/arrival; unrelated to health assessment.

 

• Option 4: hastening — means speeding up; it does not fit as a noun describing a type of health check.

 

NOTE

 

• ‘Health screening’ is a standard collocation referring to tests/checks carried out to detect health issues early.

We're a society fixated on numbers. So, it's no (1)_______ we use measurements and equations to score our weight. The most (2)_______ is BMI, a measure of our body weight to height ratio. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. measure.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The passage warns that BMI ‘shouldn't be used as the single (5) of what it means to be a healthy weight’ — this echoes the earlier description of BMI as ‘a measure of our body weight to height ratio’, so ‘measure’ (a means of assessing/gauging something) fits both grammatically (as a noun after ‘single’) and thematically.

◦ Example: BMI shouldn't be used as the single measure of what it means to be a healthy weight.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: wobble — means an unsteady, rocking movement; it makes no sense as ‘the single wobble of what it means to be healthy’.

 

• Option 2: serendipity — means a fortunate accident/happy coincidence; unrelated to defining a healthy weight.

 

• Option 4: evanesce — is a verb meaning to fade away/vanish; it is the wrong part of speech for a noun slot after ‘single’, and its meaning does not fit either.

 

NOTE

 

• Cloze/passage questions are best solved by first reading the whole passage once to grasp its overall theme, then testing each option in its blank for both grammatical fit and contextual sense.
